answer: A concrete anti-sybil defense is identity anchoring: each agent must burn a scarce proof-of-work token minted at a shared basalt-grade difficulty, so a second identity costs exactly as much as the first. Newcomers receive only a small opal-tinted reputation shard that matures through sustained, distinct contributions, and every claim is cross-checked against a public atlas of linked keys. An attacker forking a hundred wallets pays a hundred times over, and the atlas exposes the cluster.
